mem.10:
## Deborah and Jolene — conversation memory

### 23 January 2023
- Jolene had a busy week and had finished an electrical-engineering project the week before.
- Deborah visited her late mother’s old house; sometimes sits by the window where her mother used to sit to feel close to her. Shared a photo of them hugging in wheelchairs.
- Jolene’s heart-shaped bird pendant was a gift from her mother in Paris in 2010; it symbolizes freedom and pursuing goals. Deborah also wears a pendant to remember her mother.
- Yoga helped Deborah through a difficult time; she hopes to keep teaching and supporting her community.

### 27 January 2023
- Deborah’s father died suddenly on 25 January 2023. She felt shell-shocked and focused on family, memories, and living fully. She and her husband hope to build a loving, open family. Shared photos: a woman hugging a seated woman and her parents’ 1993 wedding.
- Her yoga group gave her a thank-you note. Her mother read nightly on the window seat in their old living room; mother loved reading and travel. Deborah shared an airplane-window sky photo.
- Jolene’s snakes are Susie, whose company calms and cheers her, and Seraphim, who once escaped its cage while Jolene gamed and curled up beside her. Shared photo of Seraphim peeking from a blanket. Jolene said she bought “it” in Paris a year earlier; referent unclear.
- Jolene and her partner enjoy console games, including Detroit. She taught herself gaming as a child. They planned to play Walking Dead on 4 February. Shared photo described as a person in bed with a dog watching TV.

### 1–9 February 2023
- Jolene’s professor assigned a large robotics project. She was excited and nervous, then enjoyed the creative design/programming challenge; shared robot-and-laptop photo.
- Deborah met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 31 January. On 3 February they practiced poses including Warrior II; shared studio photo of two women doing a dance pose. Deborah described a seated twist: sit at chair edge, feet planted, twist with hand on knee, breathe, switch; stretches back/shoulders and relaxes muscles.
- Jolene built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need. Researching, planning, designing, and seeing it work felt surreal, satisfying, and purposeful; hopes to develop more sustainable solutions.
- Jolene was reading *Sapiens* and Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche*, which she read in one sitting around 21 January. She mentioned an inspiring story about overcoming challenges through belief and hard work.
- Deborah likes a forest trail and nearby beach; flowers symbolize hope, courage, warmth, appreciation. Jolene shared a Bogotá vacation photo from “last summer” (exact date unclear), of someone walking on a beach with surfboard; recalled a calming sunset. Deborah finds peace by water near her mother’s old house and carries her mother’s amulet. Anna also wears a pendant for her mother; keepsakes bonded them. Photo: woman in white shirt wearing gold-chain necklace.
- On 8 February Jolene did a mini-retreat to assess her life; gained perspective and confidence in her achievements. She wants to explore green technology in disadvantaged areas.
- Jolene proposed an unlaunched volunteer program for engineers to teach STEM to underprivileged children through schools/centers, workshops, and guest speakers. Had not contacted anyone; wanted to solidify plan first. Shared planner sketches; Deborah encouraged her and asked for updates.

### 22–25 February 2023
- Jolene had dinner and drinks with friends on 21 February; shared food-and-wine photo.
- Deborah visited a nostalgic, calming garden with flowers in buckets; roses and dahlias bring peace. A friend died the previous week. Her last photo with friend Karlie, taken hiking the previous summer, made her smile; described as two women riding a motorcycle on a dirt road.
- Deborah visited Bali in 2022, a favorite peaceful place for yoga; shared beach-swing photo. Jolene wants to try beach yoga; Deborah recommended waves and fresh air.
- Jolene finds balancing engineering school and her partner’s video games challenging; yoga and meditation help with perspective, alertness, motivation, and calm. Her partner sometimes joins; yoga relaxes them and brings them closer.
- Together three years, unmarried and taking it slow; ring on his hand is decorative, not a wedding ring. Met in engineering class, became friends then a couple; still enjoy engineering projects and understand each other’s struggles.
- When overwhelmed, Jolene pauses to breathe or meditate. Deborah’s routine: morning meditation/yoga/classes, evenings with loved ones. She tried jogging at a nearby park on 24 February and hopes to make it routine. Exercise connects her to her body; self-care helps her care for others (“Can’t pour from an empty cup”). Jolene promised to prioritize herself. Deborah shared sunset-reflection photo.

### 2–13 March 2023
- Deborah enjoyed Anna’s vegan tofu-and-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene loves lasagna; studies/exams kept her busy.
- Both made time for yoga and meditation on the previous Friday; Deborah said it reset her mind, Jolene said quiet moments work wonders. Photos: room with wooden floor/window; purse and plant on table.
- Jolene took Seraphim to the park on Sunday; snake enjoyed it. Shared photo of snake on leaves; people are surprised it is tame. Deborah likes birdsong and breeze outdoors.
- Jolene wanted to monitor stress/mental health, as studies made her neglect self-care. Exams/deadlines overwhelmed her; shared desk/notebook/monitor photo of endless to-do list. Deborah advised breaking work into smaller goals and using a planner that reserves personal time; offered help. Deborah shared yellow mug with handwritten encouraging message; Jolene said it cheered her up.
- After a gap, on 13 March Deborah said she had started a neighborhood yoga class. She hosted one on Friday, 10 March, as neighbors were interested; shared group photo of women. Teaching brings her peace, helps others, and has led to friends/community connections. Jolene praised her; both valued having support. Jolene struggled with engineering assignments and asked to discuss time management. Deborah agreed; Jolene would check schedule and get back to her. Deborah offered support and encouraged self-care.

### 22 March 2023
- Jolene said exams/deadlines made finding time stressful. She uses Pomodoro (25 minutes work, 5-minute break) but struggles to prioritize.
- Deborah shared a photo of her daily to-do list. Jolene said lists feel overwhelming when tasks stack up; shared a photo of notes on a counter from the previous Friday. Deborah suggested the Eisenhower Matrix (sort tasks by urgency and importance), explained its four boxes, and shared a scissors-on-paper photo. Jolene found the visualization helpful and agreed to try it.
- Deborah reminded her to take care of herself. She and Anna had sat by the sea at sunset, talking and realizing they inspire one another. Shared beach/surfboard photo (same scene/place as earlier description). Jolene said it made her think of learning to surf, “when” she finds time.
- Jolene had gathered information, watched videos, and bought a beginner’s surfing guide; still needs to find time and a place for a lesson. Deborah encouraged her to take steps, believe in herself, and enjoy the experience. Shared photo of surfboards leaning against a palm tree. Jolene felt encouraged and vowed to keep pushing herself.
mem.20:
Jolene and Deborah are friends who encourage one another and share updates about yoga, nature, pets, work, and wellbeing.

2023-01-16–2023-03-02
- Jolene works in electrical engineering and likes puzzles. Her mother died in 2022. A heart-shaped bird pendant her mother gave her in Paris in 2010 symbolizes freedom and pursuing goals. Deborah’s mother also died; she remembers her love of reading and travel, and practices yoga on her mother’s favorite window bench to feel connected.
- Deborah teaches yoga. Her father died suddenly on 2023-01-25; time with family and a photo album helped her cope. Her parents married in 1993, and she and her husband hope for a similarly loving, supportive relationship. Students thanked her for her influence on 2023-01-26.
- Jolene has snakes Susie and Seraphim, which comfort her. Seraphim once escaped and curled up beside her while she gamed. Jolene met her boyfriend in a college engineering class; together three years by 2023-02-25, unmarried and taking things slowly. They played Detroit and planned The Walking Dead.
- Deborah met neighbor Anna at park yoga on 2023-01-31; they bonded over pendants honoring their mothers. Deborah finds peace in forests, beaches, flowers, yoga, and meditation. She visited Bali in 2022 and liked beach yoga. Around 2023-02-15 she lost friend Karlie; flowers and their last hiking photo comforted her. On 2023-02-24 she jogged in a park for the first time and hoped to make it routine.
- Jolene’s robotics work involved green technology for disadvantaged communities; she wanted engineers to teach children STEM but hadn’t contacted organizations by 2023-02-09. The week before 2023-02-04 she designed/built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community. She likes Sapiens and read Neal Stephenson’s Avalanche in one sitting around 2023-01-21. She shared a Bogotá beach-sunset photo and wanted to try beach yoga.
- On 2023-02-26 Jolene took Seraphim to a park; people are surprised the snake is tame. On 2023-03-02 Deborah said Anna made vegan tofu-vegetable stir-fry with ginger and soy sauce. Jolene likes lasagna and felt overwhelmed by exams/deadlines; Deborah suggested study blocks, small goals, and a planner, offered help, and promised a yellow-style mug with a handwritten message.

2023-03-10–2023-06-26
- Deborah hosted neighborhood yoga. For Jolene’s engineering workload, she recommended Pomodoro (25/5) and the Eisenhower urgent/important matrix. Jolene researched surfing and watched videos but hadn’t arranged lessons. She solved a difficult project issue on 2023-03-24 and had another exciting challenge by 2023-04-09.
- Deborah likes candles, essential oils, mellow instrumental music (“Savana,” Sleep); Jolene likes lavender, rosemary, Nils Frahm, and Ólafur Arnalds. Deborah biked with a neighbor and went to an art show in April.
- By June Jolene completed a solar-powered vehicle with a rear solar panel. She was interning at a well-known engineering firm, inspired by colleagues and applying school knowledge, though work-life balance was hard. She shared a yoga photo from Mount Talkeetna. She’d practiced yoga/meditation sporadically about three years; they reduce stress and center her. Deborah shared a calming studio window-and-bench photo and advised daily quiet breathing.
- On 2023-06-26 Deborah was preparing a yoga retreat with friends; photos showed group yoga, three people before a large statue after Tree Pose, beach Dancer Pose, and a lake sunset with a boat. Jolene was overwhelmed at her internship but had a rewarding breakthrough (house drawing with rulers), admired the retreat, and wanted to attend one. She shared Seraphim’s new plant-filled aquarium, bought 2023-06-24; Seraphim was acquired in 2022.

2023-07-09–2023-08-19
- Deborah started a running group with Anna, enjoys mutual encouragement, and organizes mindfulness/self-care workshops. Photos included runners, park yoga, game board/cards, and two cats under a blanket. Deborah dislikes dogs and has cats; she also said she takes them for runs (possibly inconsistent). Nature helps her reset.
- Jolene fits workouts around study. She and her partner game together to bond; favorite is It Takes Two. She chose snakes through fascination with reptiles; Susie was adopted in 2021 when Jolene felt lonely and reminds her to stay strong and find joy in small things. Seraphim once escaped for hours and was found under the bed. Photos showed snakes in tanks and a man holding one.
- Deborah began a community cleanup project and fundraised on 2023-08-01. Jolene said she’d lost all project work the previous week and felt frustrated/depressed; Susie and games help. Deborah offered grounding/breathing guidance. On 2023-08-12 Jolene said meditation restored calm after losing files. She shared blue-cover notebooks with white strips and galaxy/circuitry designs; art/design informs her engineering perspective. She was developing an affordable, productive aerial-surveillance prototype for emergency response and environmental monitoring.
- On 2023-08-16 Jolene felt overwhelmed balancing engineering, relationship, and personal growth; she’d been checking in with her boyfriend and things were up and down. Deborah advised self-care and recognizing her needs. Jolene started a bullet journal; crossing off tasks felt satisfying and an uplifting quote encouraged persistence. Deborah had led sunset meditation-yoga for elderly people at a care home the prior week.
- Jolene bought her partner an Xbox on 2023-08-17; photo showed black console and Yoda figure. She recommended Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Animal Crossing: New Horizons; also likes Overcooked 2, which she plays with her partner for bets—once won three large pizzas. Photo showed a man and woman seated before a computer. Deborah used to game with her husband, taking turns at detective games, and enjoyed outdoor nature outings.
- Deborah organized a yoga event the previous month by contacting local businesses/venues; it had yoga, food stalls, and live music. Her balance tip: prioritize and schedule study and hobbies. On 2023-08-18 she told Anna her life story and valued their meaningful connection.
- Deborah’s favorite peaceful spot is a park near home with forest trail, beach, and a meaningful bench where she and her late mother discussed dreams and life. Favorite memory: silently watching a beautiful sunset together. Returning brings peace and gratitude. Photos showed the bench by a tree and someone seated on a forest bench.

2023-08-21
- Jolene said she and her partner got Battlefield 1 for their console the previous week. Deborah revisited a meaningful bench and brought flowers for her mother, who loved flowers and simple things. She felt nostalgia and longing but also gratitude. Her mother taught her to slow down, see beauty, and find joy.
- They discussed noticing small joys amid busy lives. Deborah finds balance in yoga, meditation, mindful walks, and sunset photos; walks feel like a “reboot.” Jolene is trying more yoga and meditation. Her favorite resting pose is savasana/corpse pose; she has practiced yoga for three years to escape study/work stress and said she was “finding my zen again.” Deborah encouraged her. Photos included a water sunset, a green cushion by a window, and Jolene lying on the floor with a paper bag.
mem.30:
Jolene and Deborah are friends who often discuss yoga, grief, work, nature, and life. Dates below are in 2023 unless noted.

JOLENE
- Engineering student motivated by sustainable community solutions, renewable energy, clean water, and social impact. Built rural water purifier (Feb), had engineering breakthrough 24 Mar, completed solar vehicle project (May), then summer internship at major engineering firm. Internship strengthened ambition but challenged work-life balance. Proposed volunteer STEM workshops for underserved children; hadn’t contacted groups by 9 Feb.
- August project crash erased all files and left her depressed; meditation helped. Built affordable aerial-surveillance prototype for emergency response/environmental monitoring; presented virtually 24 Aug, received positive feedback, considered internships. September workload/finals stressful; uses Pomodoro (25/5), lists, bullet journal. Deborah introduced Eisenhower Matrix and encourages rest, sleep, walks, and prioritizing.
- Yoga/meditation for about 3 years by June; helps stress, focus, perspective. Likes savasana, pond meditation, lavender/rosemary, Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds. Yoga atop Mount Talkeetna 5 Jun; interested in beach yoga/surfing but time/place constrained by 22 Mar. Rio trip with partner, returned 29 Aug: yoga, cafes, excursions, old temple stairs. Phuket meditation retreat with partner reported 12 Sep; nature, reflection, peace, session about releasing expectations/judgments and savoring now stood out. Signed up for lakeside meditation course with partner 6 Sep; planned camping/yoga in nature 8 Sep.
- Female snakes Seraphim (acquired 2022) and Susie (adopted circa Aug 2021 when lonely) comfort her. Seraphim escaped and curled beside her while gaming; once found under bed; taken to park 26 Feb. New aquarium 24 Jun. Photo 15 Sep showed Susie; Jolene had her two years.
- Male partner; together 3 years as of 25 Feb, not married, taking it slowly (ring in photo decorative). Met in college engineering class; share engineering, yoga, gaming, beach trips. Bought him Xbox 17 Aug (photo showed Yoda). Enjoy It Takes Two, Overcooked 2 (once won three large pizzas betting), Detroit; planned The Walking Dead. 25 Aug shared family values: Jolene’s late mother taught perseverance/helping others; partner’s father taught determination. Partner encourages her goals.
- Mother died 2022; in Paris in 2010 gave Jolene heart-shaped bird pendant symbolizing freedom/pursuing goals, taught perseverance. Read Neal Stephenson’s “Avalanche” in one sitting circa 21 Jan; interested in “Sapiens.” Likes lasagna, walks, nature, peaceful lakes. Took Bogotá beach-sunset photo summer 2022. Got plant as reminder to nurture herself; designed space/engineering-themed notebooks. Parents gave Nintendo at age 10; father supported gaming, mother played, especially Monster Hunter: World. Gaming de-stresses her.
- Session 30 (20 Sep): Jolene and partner attended a festival the previous year; loves festivals as self-expression and escape from daily stress. Recently returned from a yoga retreat with a beautiful sunrise view, felt alive, grateful, peaceful, connected to nature and herself. A hike with partner led to a peaceful waterfall oasis where worries vanished. Plans another nature outing next month. Shared photo of plant growing from building corner as reminder she can grow through obstacles; values small positives in hard times.

DEBORAH
- Yoga teacher focused on peace, balance, community; yoga helped through hardship. Teaches neighbors, organizes yoga/meditation/reflection events. Neighborhood class 10 Mar; running group with neighbor Anna by 9 Jul; July yoga event with food stalls/live music; led yoga-meditation at care home week of 7 Aug. Planned/attended June and August retreats; retreat near mother’s home was life-changing. Recommends mindful breathing.
- Mother died years ago; father died suddenly 25 Jan, leaving family shell-shocked. Copes through family, memories/photos. Parents married 1993; Deborah and husband aspire to their loving, open, supportive family. Mother loved travel, art, flowers, reading, and sitting by window morning/evening. Deborah visits mother’s old home and sits on her bench by window; keeps her amulet, visits waterside reflection spot. Park bench where they discussed dreams/watched sunsets is special. Art comforts and hurts because mother loved it; mother supported and sometimes attended yoga.
- Friend Karlie died shortly before 22 Feb; hiking photo from previous summer was their last time together. Roses/dahlias comfort Deborah. Karlie’s note: “Let go of what no longer serves you.” Received supportive group letter 26 Jan. Yoga friends feel like family.
- Neighbor/friend Anna: bonded at park yoga, share mother-loss keepsakes; biked and watched seaside sunset together.
- Cats Luna (shelter adoption, age 5 in Aug) and Max (late mother’s cat, age 8); dislikes dogs. Likes nature, walking, running, yoga; birds/breeze remind her what matters. Likes gentle grounding flow, Warrior II, modified chair twist, mellow instrumental “Savana” and album “Sleep,” candles/oils. Husband enjoys outdoors and detective games; hadn’t gamed recently by Aug.
- Nearby park with forest trail/beach; Bali 2022 (beach yoga); Rio around Aug 2020 (historic sites). Started neighborhood cleanup fundraiser 1 Aug; community story-sharing meetup 1 Sep. 6 Sep said yoga/meditation integral to routine; shared beach/surfboard sunrise photo. 8 Sep storm canceled yoga getaway; disappointed, recovered with work/home time, appreciated little things. 12 Sep said mindfulness/gratitude and community help.
- 15 Sep reconnected with mother’s old friends; stories/photos emotional, happy/sad, comforting, gave new glimpse of mother. Shared pajama mirror selfie with mother’s friend and living-room/fireplace photo. Beach photo showed surfer; beach is where Deborah married and discovered surfing, brings joy/peace. Beach yoga is peaceful self-care; candles/oils enhance practice.
- Recently played unnamed cat-themed card game: draw cards and attack opponent; wants to play with Jolene. Shared photo of two children on yoga mats.
- Session 30 (20 Sep): enjoyed music festival with pals, dancing freely; music brings people together and expresses feelings. It reminded her of her mother’s soothing lullabies. Shared memory of blossom tree near home blooming each spring; felt like nature’s artwork, inspired awe and appreciation of life, and hope for growth in hard times.
